blocks.text:
Food is woven into the journey. In Santiago, you can discover contemporary Chilean cuisine. In the Atacama, enjoy a sunset cocktail, lunch amid high-altitude landscapes and a warm breakfast beside the geysers. In Patagonia, nature becomes the main attraction: glaciers, lakes and strong winds across the open spaces of Torres del Paine.

## Tour highlights

In Santiago, you can dine at Boragó, Ambrosia, Peumayen or Aquí está Coco, try seafood and dishes made with local produce, and see how contemporary cooking uses Chilean ingredients.

In the Moon Valley, the rocks of the Cordillera de la Sal turn red and gold at sunset. A chilled Pisco Sour is served as the light changes, followed after dark by a telescope session to observe the southern sky.

On the Altiplano, the route takes you to the Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, the Atacama Salt Flat and places where you can see flamingos. Lunch is served amid the high-altitude scenery.

The day at the El Tatio Geysers starts very early. At around 4,000 metres, columns of steam rise from fissures in the ground, and a warm breakfast is especially welcome in the cold air.

In Torres del Paine, a boat crosses Lake Grey past icebergs and approaches the glacier. The route then continues to lakes, lagoons, viewpoints and the 18-metre Salto Grande waterfall.
